clue.text: One particular fine place to accommodate me informally

indicators.note: the fine-plus-place pair opens up to hold the informal word for me

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a spot is a place
'us' is a colloquial British way of saying 'me', as in 'give us a kiss'

explanation.surface: Someone describes a nice spot that can put them up for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me informally' is the British colloquial 'us', as in 'give us a hand'; 'to accommodate' splits the other two pieces around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusspot is a person who is very particular, fussing over small details.

clue.text: Very delicate insect wings I am studying primarily

indicators.note: the outer letters of the insect flank, like wings, the letters placed between them

parts.note: a fly is an insect
I am contracts to I'M

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the word studying

explanation.surface: A student peers closely at the fragile wings of an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings' is a verb here: FLY flanks IM plus S, the first letter of 'studying', giving FL-IMS-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flimsy is thin and fragile, so very delicate.

clue.text: Horse drinking whiskey gets drunk

indicators.note: the horse takes the letter for whiskey inside, as if swallowing it

parts.note: a steed is a horse
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A horse that laps up whisky ends up drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewed is British slang for heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Powerful shot built up runner

parts.note: piled means heaped or built up
a river is something that runs, a common crossword riddle

explanation.surface: Someone describes an athlete who has bulked up and now strikes the ball hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete; it is a river, which runs.
explanation.definitionFit: In football or tennis a piledriver is a very forceful kick or hit.

clue.text: Skinflint provides money in an instant? The reverse all round

indicators.note: in would put the money inside the instant, giving the order the clue first proposes
this tells the solver to swap the containment, so the instant goes round inside the money instead

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money
a mo is a moment, an instant

explanation.surface: A miser's grudging way of handing over cash quickly, then reconsidering.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken at face value, 'in' puts the money inside the instant; 'The reverse all round' swaps the roles, so the instant sits inside the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens, Shakespeare's misanthrope, is used as a byword for a mean, ungenerous person.

clue.text: Large crowd welcoming back returning group

indicators.note: the crowd takes the other letters into its middle, as if welcoming them

parts.note: a mass is a large crowd

indicators.note: returning says the word end is read backwards

parts.note: the back of something is its end

explanation.surface: A huge crowd greets a band on its comeback tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group' at the end looks like part of the surface's crowd; it is the definition, a pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness is a British ska-pop band of the 1980s, a musical group.

clue.text: Give rough treatment to new worker he takes in

indicators.note: the word for he holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: he refers to a male
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A man takes on a new employee and treats him roughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he' is not a link word but stands for a male, and it is the outer piece that 'takes in' the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To manhandle someone is to push or handle them roughly.

clue.text: What smoker craves? Contrary habit!

definitions.meaning: clothing of the opposite sex, a habit being an outfit

explanation.surface: A smoker trying to quit is fighting a habit that pulls the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' suggests an addiction, but it means a garment, as a nun's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Drag is both an inhalation of smoke and cross-dressing, wearing the clothes of the other sex.

clue.text: Final chapter Poe composed with guile

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Edgar Allan Poe wrote the end of a story with cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges POE and GUILE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is a closing section added at the end of a book.

clue.text: Wisdom in place where everyone's over fifty?

parts.note: Saga is a British company offering holidays and insurance only to people over fifty
a city is a place

explanation.surface: Is wisdom found in a town full of the elderly?
explanation.walkthrough: Saga is a British company selling holidays and insurance only to people over fifty, so its customers' town would be all over-fifties.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacity is shrewd judgement and good sense.

clue.text: I carry out business model

parts.note: to deal is to trade or do business

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of running a business that is a model of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example, a model to follow.

clue.text: Authorising chap after it?

parts.note: a chap is a man
'it' is slang for sex, so someone after it is out dating

explanation.surface: A man chasing romance asks permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal or sex, so a chap 'after it' is a man dating.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandating means officially requiring or empowering, so authorising.

clue.text: 'Silence of Lambs' gets put on in Oxford theatre

parts.note: sh is a call for silence

indicators.note: in puts the word for put on inside the Lamb adjective

parts.note: Charles Lamb wrote as Elia, so Elian means of Lamb
to don a garment is to put it on

explanation.surface: A staging of The Silence of the Lambs opens in an Oxford theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the film, but the Lamb meant is the essayist Charles Lamb, who wrote as Elia; 'in' places the garment verb inside the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sheldonian Theatre is Oxford University's ceremonial hall, designed by Wren.

clue.text: Band chat on radio

indicators.note: something heard over the radio is spoken, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: to talk is to chat

explanation.surface: A band chats with a presenter on air.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent TALK and TORC sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a metal neck ring worn by ancient Celts, a band of twisted metal.

clue.text: Watch baseball player, one who's striking

parts.note: to eye is to watch
the catcher crouches behind home plate in baseball

explanation.surface: A spectator keeps an eye on a baseball player who is hitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' suggests batting; it means eye-catching.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyecatcher is someone or something that draws attention, being strikingly attractive.

clue.text: One's altogether united in disguising dirty habits

indicators.note: disguising changes the look of the letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for united, as in football team names

explanation.surface: Someone is unified in hiding their unpleasant habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguising' rearranges U with DIRTYHABITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the altogether is to be naked, wearing only the skin one was born in.

clue.text: Will reservists get involved in ordeal?

indicators.note: the reservists go inside the ordeal word, becoming involved in it

parts.note: a test can be an ordeal or trial
TA MEN are members of the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Will the reserve soldiers be put through a gruelling trial?
explanation.walkthrough: TA is Britain's Territorial Army, so TA MEN are reservists; they go inside TEST as TES-TAMEN-T. 'Will' is the noun, a testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document passing on property after death.

clue.text: Rogue broadcast not up to scratch

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rogue
aired means broadcast

explanation.surface: A rascal's TV show is broadcast and judged substandard.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired means weakened or damaged, so below normal standard.

clue.text: What embarassment is making girl hide?

parts.note: a miss is a girl
a pelt is an animal hide

explanation.surface: Asking what shame makes a girl want to hide away.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue itself spells 'embarrassment' wrongly with one R, so the definition describes its own word. 'hide' is a noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed 'embarassment' lacks an R, so it is spelt wrongly: a self-referential definition.

clue.text: Economical over, one delivered on stump possibly, in debut at Lords?

parts.note: in cricket a maiden over is one from which no runs are scored, the most economical kind
a speech is delivered, and politicians speak 'on the stump' when campaigning

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: a tight over and a ball hitting the stumps at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, Lord's being London's great cricket ground; but Lords is the House of Lords, and 'on the stump' means campaigning on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden speech is a member's first address to Parliament, including the House of Lords.

clue.text: Guard nuclear bunker?

parts.note: the word nuclear pairs with war, so a nuclear bunker is a shelter for war
a den is a hideaway or shelter

explanation.surface: A guard stands watch over a fallout shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: A nuclear bunker is read as a den for (nuclear) war.
explanation.definitionFit: A warden is a custodian or keeper, such as a prison guard.

clue.text: Expression to introduce unknown belief not widely accepted

parts.note: 'here's' is said when introducing someone, as in 'here's John'
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Someone presents an unorthodox idea for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is an opinion contrary to orthodox doctrine, rejected by most.

clue.text: Primate securing small niche

indicators.note: the primate holds the letter for small inside, securing it

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey grabs a little hollow to sit in.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a recess at the end of a church, a vaulted niche.

clue.text: Rail coach carrying the French turned over business

indicators.note: the coach holds the other letters inside it, carrying them

parts.note: a coach is a bus

indicators.note: turned over says the French word is written backwards

parts.note: la is French for the
trade is business

explanation.surface: A rail firm with a French coach operator has a busy turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' applies only to the French article, which then sits inside the coach; 'Rail' is the definition, not a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A balustrade is a railing supported by balusters, as on a staircase or balcony.

clue.text: Surprising result riding on clot

parts.note: a jockey who is up is riding the horse
to set is to clot or solidify

explanation.surface: A shock win for a horse with a dim jockey aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clot' looks like an insult for a fool; it is a verb, to congeal.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset in sport is an unexpected win by the underdog.

clue.text: Terrorist group carrying pounds in old money

indicators.note: the group bears the pounds letter, which sits at its head in the answer

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra
the IRA is the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: Paramilitaries carry cash in an outdated currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' here puts L before IRA, as if the group were holding it up front.

clue.text: Poor quality of voice is sneered about

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are scattered around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's bad singing is mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ISSNEERED.
explanation.definitionFit: A reedy voice is thin and high, so reediness is that weak tone.

clue.text: Some wretched gents act shiftily

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few miserable men behave evasively.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedge is to avoid committing oneself, being evasive.

clue.text: Take away tons transported back

indicators.note: back says the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: carted means transported

explanation.surface: Tons of goods are hauled back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses TCARTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract is to diminish, taking away from the value of something.

clue.text: Radio bringing in leader of Yemen's despotic regime

indicators.note: the radio word takes the letter inside itself

parts.note: tranny is dated British slang for a transistor radio

indicators.note: leader of asks for the first letter of Yemen

explanation.surface: State radio announces the ruler of Yemen's harsh government.
